provider: Arweave via ar.io / Turbo (ario-deploy free tier)

free_tier.stated: Turbo free tier: 105 KiB per data item, 10 MiB over the lifetime of a wallet AND 10 MiB over the lifetime of an IP range. Larger files are billed.

egress.terms: Arweave reads are effectively unmetered through gateways (arweave.net, ar.io gateways) — genuinely free egress, which is why this would otherwise be interesting. But there is nothing to serve.

tooling: ario-deploy CLI, Turbo SDK (@ardriveapp/turbo-sdk), ar.io SDK; arbundles/Irys for direct bundling.
chaining: Actively defeated by design: the IP-range meter means the entire free allowance for a datacenter is shared. 'ario-deploy can check the wallet's allowance... It cannot check the IP range, so a deploy can pass the credit check and still be refused at upload time with HTTP 402 when other people on the same network have used the range's allowance.'
limits_note: 105 KiB/file; 10 MiB/wallet lifetime; 10 MiB/IP-range lifetime; HTTP 402 past that.
reliability_note: The IP-range metering is the anti-farming mechanism, and it works: this is the one design in the class that explicitly anticipates the 'unlimited wallets' move. Confirms the prior agent's finding, with the mechanism spelled out (dual metering, wallet + range, 402 on the range).
confidence_note: One page read moves it to documented.

evidence.proved: '105 KiB per file (per data item)'; '10 MiB over the lifetime of a wallet, and 10 MiB over the lifetime of an IP range. Turbo meters both'

notes: Turbo free tier: 105 KiB per data item, 10 MiB over the lifetime of a wallet AND 10 MiB over the lifetime of an IP range. Larger files are billed.

extras.unit_note: free_tier.unit is 'mixed' because the headline is denominated in MiB or KiB, which the schema enum does not carry; the verbatim free_tier.stated keeps the true unit. See the storage-dossier handover.

binding_note: the per-object cap sets the shard size and therefore the object count; it bounds the total more tightly than any headline quota
